mintAuthority.summary: USDT is issuer-minted by Tether; on Ethereum the token owner is a 3/6 legacy multisig-style owner set with direct supply authority.

mintIncidents.summary: During an Omni-to-Tron chain swap, Tether accidentally minted 5B USDT instead of the intended 50M, then burned the excess supply to restore the intended issuance.

controls.label: Ethereum USDT token owner multisig
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095839, USDT owner() and getOwner() returned this address; deprecated() and paused() were false. The owner contract returned required() = 3 and six owners. Verified USDT source gives that owner unrestricted issue(uint256) and deprecate(address) authority; the verified owner is a legacy MultiSigWallet, so Safe modules and guards do not apply. This control and its custom migration authority are verified for Ethereum only, not for native deployments on other chains.

controls.evidence: At finalized Solana slot 452216277, getMultipleAccounts read the canonical USDT mint and this authority in one response. The mint's mintAuthority and freezeAuthority were both this address. Both accounts were owned by the original SPL Token Program (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA); the authority parsed as an initialized multisig with numRequiredSigners = 2 and numValidSigners = 3. Its members were 66YZZejVBupBnMwSEqTaCkAMwPacpPzP41GSEst55Kgz, yo4bccTt3FTnMguy2D3NCox8tG1CuHYRfxAdQoiJ7Th, and A3znyaRYUvi7GbQv1pp9CqqiVo7anddU9rPKFH55V28R. This verifies direct mint/freeze authority, not upgrade or migration authority.

sources.label: Tether announces KPMG U.S. annual financial-statement audit, 2026-08-13

review.evidence: Ethereum block 26095839 confirms the current 3-of-6 owner multisig and an unrestricted owner-only issue path on Ethereum; the upgradeability record is scoped to that deployment only. The existing 2019 accidental 5B issuance remains recorded as resolved. Tether publishes daily circulation information and quarterly reserve assurance reports, supporting periodic reconciliation. Tether separately announced a KPMG U.S. audit of its 2025 financial statements on 2026-08-13; a financial-statement audit is not evidence of prudential supervision of minting.
